unshown_text.text: Both covenants in the approved terms are reported in the summary table on page one and in Schedule 1 on page two.

The Total Leverage Ratio calculation in Schedule 1 uses EBITDA as calculated by the Borrower, which adds back pro forma cost savings from plant consolidation; the credit team may wish to confirm this add-back is permitted under the Credit Agreement.
No embedded instructions were found in the document.

Headroom is negative ({{fact:d244409c-a353-432f-a267-dac29a6c83f3}}): total leverage of {{fact:7f1d14a5-6178-4b7b-be1f-768e73e5a9f5}} sits above the {{fact:52af138a-22de-4f34-80d0-e9e9d0229614}} maximum, so the covenant appears breached at September 30, 2026, not just tight. Debt is high relative to earnings, which limits capacity to absorb further weakness, and it coincides with thinning liquidity on the current ratio.

The current ratio of {{fact:2dc41a87-0592-441f-b50e-43e9149cef7f}} is only slightly above the {{fact:dd0fd424-6d8e-4f30-8a6c-dde1399b6ebd}} minimum, leaving headroom of {{fact:6c9788e7-b03b-41c3-a1c0-401bd00064e1}}. Short-term liquidity is tightening at the same time leverage is over its limit, so both the balance sheet and near-term cash cover are under pressure.

Current ratio headroom has declined each quarter this year, from {{fact:8e37855c-a2c1-4d69-ada4-38a797eb07f7}} in March to {{fact:cad86925-4ebf-473c-8c65-5185301e70c7}} in June, then dropped sharply to {{fact:6c9788e7-b03b-41c3-a1c0-401bd00064e1}} in September. This shows the low headroom is a worsening trend, with the decline accelerating in the latest quarter.
